title: SLO vs Burn decision session - Mirador Labs
summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics vs latency SLOs. Mirador is evaluating hosted -> dedicated -> private path; main constraints are a $25k/month budget for inference, 150ms 95th pct latency target for user-facing prompts, and strict SOC2 compliance. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot scoped to 1k qps burst with sample prompts, Redwood to send cost model spreadsheet and SSO/security pack.
topics: impact of batching and KV (prefix) caching
deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private
pilot scope, timeline, and success criteria
action_items: Ethan Brooks | Send detailed hosted vs dedicated cost model spreadsheet with sample workload rows and batching assumptions | 2027-04-25
Sara Kim | Prepare short benchmark guide for KV-cache effects and recommended batching parameters for Mirador prompts | 2027-04-26
Ana Ruiz | Share 3 representative prompt sets and average token lengths for user-facing and background tasks | 2027-04-23
Kevin O'Leary | Confirm regulatory contact and SSO/KMS constraints (do we need HSM?) | 2027-04-27
next_steps: Redwood to model cost scenarios (hosted/dedicated/private) using customer's prompt samples
Customer to provide prompt samples and current telemetry for token lengths
Schedule 30m pilot kickoff once samples received (target week of 2027-05-03)

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-04-22
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (AE, Redwood), Sara (SE, Redwood), Ana (Head of ML, Mirador), Kevin (CTO, Mirador), Jules (SRE, Mirador)

[00:00] Ethan: ok hi everybody thanks for joining on a Thursday afternoon, appreciate it. quick introductions?
[00:09] Ana: hi yeah I'm Ana, head of ML at Mirador. we run most of our user facing NLP features inhouse; right now it's on prem with some cloud bursts.
[00:18] Kevin: Kevin here, CTO. budget is a hard ceiling — we're looking at roughly $25k / month for inference initially.
[00:25] Jules: Jules, platform, I'll be owning the deployment and network pieces.
[00:29] Ethan: great. Sara is our solutions engineer — she'll go through some of the tradeoffs and numbers.
[00:35] Sara: hi all. quick agenda — understand your stack and constraints, talk per-token economics, describe batching and prefix/KV cache levers, and go over deployment options and security. any changes?
[00:46] Ana: sounds good. I want to make sure we can hit a 95th pct latency of ~150ms for user prompts; background jobs can be slower.
[00:54] Ethan: noted — so low latency for interactive pieces is a primary SLO. also confirm: SOC2 is required?
[00:59] Kevin: yes SOC2 and need SSO via SAML, plus customer-managed KMS ideally. we can consider HSM later.
[01:08] Sara: good to know. on the cost side, per-token pricing will vary by model — open heavy models cost more compute per token. we compare hosted per-token list prices vs dedicated committed capacity which changes unit economics.
[01:23] Ana: when you say dedicated committed capacity, is that like reserved GPUs with a predictable rate and lower per-token?
[01:29] Sara: exactly — Dedicated is effectively reserved capacity; you pay for the pool monthly but get much lower per-token run time since scheduling overhead and multi-tenant tax are reduced. caching and batching also amplify that.
[01:39] Ethan: quick aside — sometimes transcripts will say "Redwood Dedicate" — sorry, that was a tongue twister — the product is Redwood Dedicated.
[01:46] Jules: ha. ok. can you walk through an example? our median prompt token length is ~60 tokens, user-facing. background inference is 240 tokens.
[01:55] Sara: sure. example scenario: hosted using a mid-size open model — let's assume 0.6ms/token GPU time (this is illustrative). at small qps, per-token cost includes overheads; with batching of ~8 we'll amortize overheads and get ~0.45ms/token effective. with KV-cache for our user prompts (we saw many shared prefixes) you can cut generation time by maybe 30% because of prefix reuse.
[02:17] Ana: so caching helps a lot for our chat-like flows. how often would you need cache hits to be worth it?
[02:22] Sara: if you see 15-20% prefix reuse that's already meaningful; at 40% reuse it's a game-changer. note that cache efficacy depends on prompt formatting and whether you send full context each time.
[02:33] Kevin: latency concerns — if we batch too much to reduce cost, does that push us over the 150ms 95th?
[02:40] Sara: yes that's the tradeoff — batching improves throughput and lowers per-token cost, but per-request tail latency can increase. Redwood supports adaptive batching with latency SLOs: you set a max acceptable latency and we batch under that constraint.
[02:52] Ethan: we also have routing policies — critical calls can be routed to a low-latency pool (dedicated) and cheaper calls to a burst or lower tier. that lets you keep important SLOs while optimizing cost.
[03:03] Ana: the budget is tight — can you sketch a pilot we can run to validate numbers?
[03:09] Sara: yes — typical pilot: you give us three representative prompt sets + qps/traffic windows. we run a 2-week pilot in hosted or dedicated (your choice) with controlled load, measure token counts, latency percentiles, cache hit rates. Redwood will return a CSV with modeled per-token numbers for hosted, dedicated w/commit, and a private deployment estimate.
[03:28] Jules: for private/on-prem what changes? do we still get your console for metrics?
[03:33] Ethan: private includes a control plane that can be customer-managed; the console can be run in an air-gapped mode or via a private connectivity link depending on the package. there are more integration steps (network, KMS) and licensing fees. unit costs are typically higher for small scale but you gain data residency and control.
[03:49] Kevin: any red flags on compliance? we need KMS and SSO and an audit log stream we can pull into our SIEM.
[03:56] Sara: we integrate with major KMS providers and support SAML for SSO. audit logs are available; we can set up a push to your Splunk/Datadog using a secure forwarder. we'll include SOC2 docs in the security pack.
[04:09] Ana: about model choice — we're debating between an open LLaMA-ish variant vs a distilled model; how does that affect per-token cost?
[04:16] Sara: model size matters — bigger models use more GPU cycles per token. Distilled or quantized variants can be up to 3-4x cheaper per token but might lose quality. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles by workload; for retrieval-augmented prompts you often don't need the largest model.
[04:33] Kevin: does Redwood have a way to automatically fallback if capacity is constrained?
[04:37] Ethan: yes — automatic fallback policies can route to a compatible smaller model or to a different region/instance tier. we can define per-route policies and prioritize by SLA.
[04:47] Jules: operationally, we need to know how autoscaling and burst capacity are billed for dedicated. is burst billed separately?
[04:53] Sara: burst capacity is optional; for dedicated you reserve a baseline pool and can configure burst tiers that spin up extra capacity billed at a higher short-term rate. in the spreadsheet we'll show both amortized and on-demand burst numbers.
[05:05] Ana: what's the typical unit from your hosted price list? tokens? per-token per-1k tokens?
[05:10] Ethan: typically we publish per-1k-token units for completions plus an embedding unit where relevant. in the model-level sheet we'll show per-1k tokens and translate to per-request numbers using your average token length.
[05:21] Kevin: timeline — we want a pilot in May. can you support a quick kickoff?
[05:25] Sara: yes if you send prompt samples and expected qps by next Tues we can provision and start the pilot week of 2027-05-03. pilot run will be 14 days with mid-pilot check-in.
[05:36] Ana: ok I'll get the prompt sets over. one more thing — logging and PII handling. we do not want raw user messages stored off-site. is there an option for ephemeral logs?
[05:46] Ethan: for hosted we can configure no-persist or limited retention. dedicated/private gives you stronger controls. we'll note that in the security pack.
[05:55] Jules: network — do you support VPC peering or private link?
[06:00] Sara: yes both options depending on region; for private we do customer-managed networking.
[06:05] Kevin: any immediate upsides to starting hosted pilot vs deploying dedicated from day one? I'm weighing speed vs cost.
[06:12] Sara: hosted is fastest to start and gives you real metrics to model cost. Dedicated reduces per-token cost with the commitment but requires more ops lead time. many teams do hosted pilot then convert to dedicated once they have stable traffic and SLOs.
[06:26] Ethan: to summarize — Redwood will: send pricing/cost-model spreadsheet, send SOC2/security pack + SSO/KMS integration notes, and S E will prepare KV-cache and batching benchmark notes. Mirador will: send prompt samples and confirm internal security contact.
[06:40] Ana: good recap. can we also get an illustrative example line item for 50k user prompts/day?
[06:45] Sara: yes we'll include a sample row showing token math, batching assumptions, cache hit rate scenarios.
[06:52] Kevin: thanks all. any blockers?
[06:55] Jules: none from infra besides getting the CIDR ranges for peering but that's after pilot scope.
[07:01] Ethan: great — we'll follow up with emails and attach the docs. thanks for your time.

End of transcript.
